title: Goddess’s Day or Women’s Day?
synopsis: One of the criticisms of Women’s Day in China comes from its Chinese name.

fullText.simplified:
女神节还是妇女节？
    三月八号快到了，这一天是“国际妇女节”，是个属于全世界女性的节日。很多男性都会在这一天给身边的女性家人和朋友送去祝福，以此来表达他们的敬意和感激。这不但是个和谐的日子，也是个“有爱”的日子。
    “国际妇女节”在中国已有近百年历史，一直都是个受欢迎的节日。但近几年，随着社会和经济的飞速发展，人们对这个节日的称呼有了一些变化，好像变得没有以前那么爽快了。为什么会有这种变化呢？原因就在“妇女”这两个字上。
    “妇女”在汉语词典里的意思是指成年的女性，就是十八岁和十八岁以上的女性。所有成年的女性，不管是已经结婚，还是没有结婚的女性，都可以称为“妇女”。但是，这只是词典里的解释，现在的实际情况是，如果你称一个没有结婚的女性为“妇女”，这恐怕是件特别糟糕的事情。在现代人的印象中，“妇女”更多是指结了婚的女性。对着一个年轻或是没有结婚的女性叫“妇女”，你会收到一个大大的白眼。
    不但没有结婚的女性不喜欢被人称为“妇女”，结了婚的女性其实也不喜欢被人称为“妇女”。这又是为什么呢？原因还是在称呼上，因为这个“妇”字。如果用“妇”字组词，你能想到哪些词呢？媳妇，主妇，妇人……这些词都是名词，是指不同身份的女性。这些女性在传统观念中都有一个相同的特点，就是持家，做大量的家务，一生为家人而劳作。在以前，这不仅是正常现象，还是对传统女性美德的一种歌颂。但现在呢？现在还是这样吗？
    “妇女节”在中国已有百年历史，现今中国女性的地位和百年前相比，已经发生了显著的变化，很多人的思想观念也发生了变化。相较于以前的持家顺从，现代已婚女性更崇尚独立和自由。虽然她们同样爱家、照顾家人，但她们不愿意再像旧时代女性那样被过时的规则所束缚。她们不喜欢被定义，尤其不喜欢被“妇”字所代表的传统身份所定义，她们追求更自我的人生。
    很多人已经注意到了这种思想观念的巨大转变，因此顺应潮流地将“妇女节”换了一种称呼，“女生节”、“女王节”和“女神节”都是应运而生的新称呼。这其中，似乎“女神节”最受人欢迎。因此在三月八号那天，你能听到很多中国女性收到“女神节快乐”这样的祝福。
    当然，任何事情都会有不同的声音。在新称呼受人欢迎的同时，也有人提出了反对的意见。持反对意见的人认为，相较于真正的理解和尊重，“女生节”、“女王节”和“女神节”这些都只是一种浮于表面的称谓。一个真正独立和自强的女性，是不会为任何虚浮的称呼所影响，更不会为它们所定义。所以，与其追求这些称谓上的虚荣，还不如保持本我，接受一句“妇女节快乐”又有何不可呢？
    归根到底，不管是“女神节”，还是“妇女节”，背后反映的其实都是新时代女性的新思维，这都是好事。如果你有来自中国的女性朋友，在三月八号这一天，你想对她说什么呢？

女神節還是婦女節？
    三月八號快到了，這一天是“國際婦女節”，是個屬於全世界女性的節日。很多男性都會在這一天給身邊的女性家人和朋友送去祝福，以此來表達他們的敬意和感激。這不但是個和諧的日子，也是個“有愛”的日子。
    “國際婦女節”在中國已有近百年歷史，一直都是個受歡迎的節日。但近幾年，隨著社會和經濟的飛速發展，人們對這個節日的稱呼有了一些變化，好像變得沒有以前那麼爽快了。為什麼會有這種變化呢？原因就在“婦女”這兩個字上。
    “婦女”在漢語詞典裡的意思是指成年的女性，就是十八歲和十八歲以上的女性。所有成年的女性，不管是已經結婚，還是沒有結婚的女性，都可以稱為“婦女”。但是，這只是詞典裡的解釋，現在的實際情況是，如果你稱一個沒有結婚的女性為“婦女”，這恐怕是件特別糟糕的事情。在現代人的印象中，“婦女”更多是指結了婚的女性。對著一個年輕或是沒有結婚的女性叫“婦女”，你會收到一個大大的白眼。
    不但沒有結婚的女性不喜歡被人稱為“婦女”，結了婚的女性其實也不喜歡被人稱為“婦女”。這又是為什麼呢？原因還是在稱呼上，因為這個“婦”字。如果用“婦”字組詞，你能想到哪些詞呢？媳婦，主婦，婦人……這些詞都是名詞，是指不同身份的女性。這些女性在傳統觀念中都有一個相同的特點，就是持家，做大量的家務，一生為家人而勞作。在以前，這不僅是正常現象，還是對傳統女性美德的一種歌頌。但現在呢？現在還是這樣嗎？
    “婦女節”在中國已有百年歷史，現今中國女性的地位和百年前相比，已經發生了顯著的變化，很多人的思想觀念也發生了變化。相較於以前的持家順從，現代已婚女性更崇尚獨立和自由。雖然她們同樣愛家、照顧家人，但她們不願意再像舊時代女性那樣被過時的規則所束縛。她們不喜歡被定義，尤其不喜歡被“婦”字所代表的傳統身份所定義，她們追求更自我的人生。
    很多人已經注意到了這種思想觀念的巨大轉變，因此順應潮流地將“婦女節”換了一種稱呼，“女生節”、“女王節”和“女神節”都是應運而生的新稱呼。這其中，似乎“女神節”最受人歡迎。因此在三月八號那天，你能聽到很多中國女性收到“女神節快樂”這樣的祝福。
    當然，任何事情都會有不同的聲音。在新稱呼受人歡迎的同時，也有人提出了反對的意見。持反對意見的人認為，相較於真正的理解和尊重，“女生節”、“女王節”和“女神節”這些都只是一種浮於表面的稱謂。一個真正獨立和自強的女性，是不會為任何虛浮的稱呼所影響，更不會為它們所定義。所以，與其追求這些稱謂上的虛榮，還不如保持本我，接受一句“婦女節快樂”又有何不可呢？
    歸根到底，不管是“女神節”，還是“婦女節”，背後反映的其實都是新時代女性的新思維，這都是好事。如果你有來自中國的女性朋友，在三月八號這一天，你想對她說什麼呢？

sentences.traditional: 她們追求更自我的人生。
sentences.pinyin: tā men zhuī qiú gèng zì wǒ de rén shēng
sentences.english: They don’t like to be defined, especially by the traditional identity represented by the character “fu”, ..
.. and they seek a life that is more for themselves.

sentences.simplified: 很多人已经注意到了这种思想观念的巨大转变，因此顺应潮流地将“妇女节”换了一种称呼，
sentences.traditional: 很多人已經注意到了這種思想觀念的巨大轉變，因此順應潮流地將“婦女節”換了一種稱呼，
sentences.pinyin: hěn duō rén yǐ jīng zhù yì dào le zhè zhǒng sī xiǎng guān niàn de jù dà zhuǎn biàn yīn cǐ shùn yìng cháo liú de jiāng fù nǚ jié huàn le yì zhǒng chēng hu

sentences.simplified: “女生节”、“女王节”和“女神节”都是应运而生的新称呼。
sentences.traditional: “女生節”、“女王節”和“女神節”都是應運而生的新稱呼。
sentences.pinyin: nǚ shēng jié nǚ wáng jié hé nǚ shén jié dōu shì yìng yùn ér shēng de xīn chēng hu
sentences.english: Many people have noticed this huge change in thinking, so they have changed the name of “Women’s Day” in line with the trend.

sentences.simplified: 这其中，似乎“女神节”最受人欢迎。
sentences.traditional: 這其中，似乎“女神節”最受人歡迎。
sentences.pinyin: zhè qí zhōng sì hū nǚ shén jié zuì shòu rén huān yíng
sentences.english: “Girls’ Day”, “Queens’ Day”, and “Goddess’s Day” are all new names that have emerged in response.

sentences.simplified: 因此在三月八号那天，你能听到很多中国女性收到“女神节快乐”这样的祝福。
sentences.traditional: 因此在三月八號那天，你能聽到很多中國女性收到“女神節快樂”這樣的祝福。
sentences.pinyin: yīn cǐ zài sān yuè bā hào nà tiān nǐ néng tīng dào hěn duō zhōng guó nǚ xìng shōu dào nǚ shén jié kuài lè zhè yàng de zhù fú
sentences.english: Among them, it seems that “Goddess’s Day” is the most popular.
So on March 8th, you can hear many Chinese women receiving good wishes such as “Happy Goddess’s Day”.

sentences.simplified: 当然，任何事情都会有不同的声音。
sentences.traditional: 當然，任何事情都會有不同的聲音。
sentences.pinyin: dāng rán rèn hé shì qing dōu huì yǒu bù tóng de shēng yīn

sentences.simplified: 在新称呼受人欢迎的同时，也有人提出了反对的意见。
sentences.traditional: 在新稱呼受人歡迎的同時，也有人提出了反對的意見。
sentences.pinyin: zài xīn chēng hu shòu rén huān yíng de tóng shí yě yǒu rén tí chū le fǎn duì de yì jiàn
sentences.english: Of course, people will voice different opinions on everything.

sentences.simplified: 持反对意见的人认为，相较于真正的理解和尊重，
sentences.traditional: 持反對意見的人認為，相較於真正的理解和尊重，
sentences.pinyin: chí fǎn duì yì jiàn de rén rèn wéi xiāng jiào yú zhēn zhèng de lǐ jiě hé zūn zhòng
sentences.english: While the new names were well received, there were also objections raised.

sentences.simplified: “女生节”、“女王节”和“女神节”这些都只是一种浮于表面的称谓。
sentences.traditional: “女生節”、“女王節”和“女神節”這些都只是一種浮於表面的稱謂。
sentences.pinyin: nǚ shēng jié nǚ wáng jié hé nǚ shén jié zhè xiē dōu zhǐ shì yì zhǒng fú yú biǎo miàn de chēng wèi
sentences.english: Opponents argue that compared to true understanding and respect, ..

sentences.simplified: 一个真正独立和自强的女性，是不会为任何虚浮的称呼所影响，更不会为它们所定义。
sentences.traditional: 一個真正獨立和自強的女性，是不會為任何虛浮的稱呼所影響，更不會為它們所定義。
sentences.pinyin: yí ge zhēn zhèng dú lì hé zì qiáng de nǚ xìng shì bú huì wèi rèn hé xū fú de chēng hu suǒ yǐng xiǎng gèng bú huì wèi tā men suǒ dìng yì
sentences.english: .. “Girls’ Day”, “Queens’ Day”, and “Goddess’s Day” are just superficial names.

sentences.simplified: 所以，与其追求这些称谓上的虚荣，还不如保持本我，接受一句“妇女节快乐”又有何不可呢？
sentences.traditional: 所以，與其追求這些稱謂上的虛榮，還不如保持本我，接受一句“婦女節快樂”又有何不可呢？
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ yǔ qí zhuī qiú zhè xiē chēng wèi shang de xū róng hái bù rú bǎo chí běn wǒ jiē shòu yí jù fù nǚ jié kuài lè yòu yǒu hé bù kě ne
sentences.english: A truly independent and self-empowered woman is not influenced by, let alone defined by, any superficial name.
So, instead of pursuing the vanity of these names, why not stay true to yourself and accept a “Happy Women’s Day”?

sentences.simplified: 归根到底，不管是“女神节”，还是“妇女节”，
sentences.traditional: 歸根到底，不管是“女神節”，還是“婦女節”，
sentences.pinyin: guī gēn dào dǐ bù guǎn shì nǚ shén jié hái shi fù nǚ jié

sentences.simplified: 背后反映的其实都是新时代女性的新思维，这都是好事。
sentences.traditional: 背後反映的其實都是新時代女性的新思維，這都是好事。
sentences.pinyin: bèi hòu fǎn yìng de qí shí dōu shì xīn shí dài nǚ xìng de xīn sī wéi zhè dōu shì hǎo shì
sentences.english: In the end, whether it’s “Goddess’s Day” or “Women’s Day”, ..

sentences.simplified: 如果你有来自中国的女性朋友，在三月八号这一天，你想对她说什么呢？
sentences.traditional: 如果你有來自中國的女性朋友，在三月八號這一天，你想對她說什麼呢？
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ nǐ yǒu lái zì zhōng guó de nǚ xìng péng you zài sān yuè bā hào zhè yì tiān nǐ xiǎng duì tā shuō shén me ne
sentences.english: .. behind it is actually the new thinking of women in the new era, which is a good thing.

sentence_translations: Goddess’s Day or Women’s Day?
March 8th is coming up. This day is International Women’s Day, a holiday that belongs to women all over the world.
Many men show their respect and gratitude by sending blessings to female family and friends around them on this day.
It is not only a day of harmony but also a day of “love”.
“International Women’s Day” has been a popular holiday in China for nearly a hundred years.
However, in recent years, with rapid social and economic development, ..
.. there have been some changes to the name of this holiday, and it seems to have become less straightforward than before.
Why this change? The reason is the two characters, “fu nü”.
The meaning of “fu nü” in a Chinese dictionary refers to an adult female, that is, a female aged 18 and above.
All adult women, regardless of whether they are married or unmarried, can be called “fu nü”.
But that’s just a dictionary explanation.
The reality nowadays is that if you call an unmarried woman “fu nü”, that would be a very bad thing.
In the minds of modern people, “fu nü” more often refers to married women.
Call a young or unmarried woman “fu nü”, and you’ll get a big eye roll.
Not only do women who are not married dislike being called “fu nü”, ..
.. but women who are married actually also dislike being called “fu nü”.
And why is that? The reason is still in the name. It’s because of the character “fu”.
If you use the character “fu” to form words, what words can you think of?
The words daughter-in-law, housewife, and married woman … are all nouns that refer to women in different capacities.
In the traditional way of thinking, these women all share the same characteristic ..
.. of being housekeepers, doing a lot of housework, and working for their families their entire lives.
In the past, this was not only the norm but also praised as traditional female virtue.
But what about now? Is it still the case?
“Women’s Day” has been celebrated in China for a hundred years.
The status of women in China today has changed significantly from what it was a hundred years ago, ..
.. and many people’s mindsets have changed as well.
Compared to the domestic submissiveness of the past, modern married women hold independence and freedom in higher esteem.
Although they love their homes and take care of their families just as much, ..
.. they are no longer willing to be bound by outdated rules as women were in the old days.
They don’t like to be defined, especially by the traditional identity represented by the character “fu”, ..
.. and they seek a life that is more for themselves.
Many people have noticed this huge change in thinking, so they have changed the name of “Women’s Day” in line with the trend.
“Girls’ Day”, “Queens’ Day”, and “Goddess’s Day” are all new names that have emerged in response.
Among them, it seems that “Goddess’s Day” is the most popular.
So on March 8th, you can hear many Chinese women receiving good wishes such as “Happy Goddess’s Day”.
Of course, people will voice different opinions on everything.
While the new names were well received, there were also objections raised.
Opponents argue that compared to true understanding and respect, ..
.. “Girls’ Day”, “Queens’ Day”, and “Goddess’s Day” are just superficial names.
A truly independent and self-empowered woman is not influenced by, let alone defined by, any superficial name.
So, instead of pursuing the vanity of these names, why not stay true to yourself and accept a “Happy Women’s Day”?
